title: Ingrown toenail
intro: An ingrown toenail occurs when the edge of a nail grows into the surrounding skin, causing pain, redness and sometimes infection. It most often affects the big toe. Simple home care works in mild cases, while recurrent or infected nails may need a small procedure.

sections.heading: Causes
paragraphs: Common causes include cutting nails too short or rounding the corners, tight shoes, injury, sweaty feet and naturally curved nails. Some people have a family tendency. Teenagers and people who do a lot of running or football are often affected.

sections.heading: Symptoms
paragraphs: The skin beside the nail becomes tender, red and swollen. Walking and wearing shoes may hurt. If the skin becomes infected, there may be pus, throbbing pain and the area may grow soft tissue called granulation tissue.

sections.heading: Self-care in early stages
paragraphs: Soak the foot in warm water several times a day, dry it carefully and gently push the skin away from the nail edge. Wear roomy shoes or sandals and keep the area clean. Cut nails straight across in the future, and do not dig at the corner with sharp tools. Over-the-counter pain relievers can be used as directed.

sections.heading: Medical treatment
paragraphs: If the nail does not improve, is very painful or infected, see a doctor or podiatrist. They may lift the nail edge and place a small splint, trim the ingrown part under local anaesthetic, or prescribe antibiotics for infection. For repeated problems, a minor operation can remove part of the nail and treat the root so that it does not grow back at the edges. Healing usually takes a few weeks.

sections.heading: Prevention and special cases
paragraphs: Choose well-fitting shoes with space for the toes and trim nails properly. People with diabetes, poor circulation or numb feet should see a professional early and not treat the problem themselves, because infections can become serious quickly. Seek urgent care for spreading redness, fever or a black or very swollen toe.

examples.title: Treating it early
examples.text: Imagine the edge of your toenail is sore after a long walk in tight shoes. You could switch to roomy shoes, soak your foot in warm water daily and see a podiatrist if the pain does not improve in a few days.

examples.title: Planning a procedure
examples.text: Suppose you have had the same nail ingrown several times. You might ask about a small operation, what the recovery involves and how long you should avoid sports.
